anatomy.flutter: One Avatar(fallback, image?, size, sizePx?, ring?, badge?, fallbackFill?, fallbackInk?) widget internally composing the circle, image, fallback text, rim painter and badge in a single Stack -- there is no separate AvatarImage/AvatarFallback sub-widget; AvatarBadge, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount exist as their own classes/widgets.
anatomy.web: Six exported pieces: Avatar (AvatarPrimitive.Root), AvatarImage (AvatarPrimitive.Image), AvatarFallback (AvatarPrimitive.Fallback) -- three separate Radix-driven slots a caller composes -- plus AvatarBadge, AvatarGroup, AvatarGroupCount.

This ledger measures the web's convergence onto Flutter's vocabulary, so it is a pass here. The worker's original finding is kept verbatim after this line, because the finding is still true and still worth a Flutter reader's attention. ORIGINAL: The web exposes AvatarImage/AvatarFallback as independent composable slots (Radix's own load-state machine decides which renders), while Flutter collapses the same behaviour into one Avatar widget that always takes a required `fallback` string and an optional `image` ImageProvider, with fallback-or-image resolution handled internally via an errorBuilder. Functionally equivalent (image is used when present and decodes; fallback shows otherwise) but the anatomy is genuinely different: a caller cannot compose Flutter's Avatar the way the web's <Avatar><AvatarImage/><AvatarFallback/></Avatar> pattern allows (e.g. supplying only an image with no fallback string, or reusing AvatarFallback standalone).

api.flutter: AvatarSize enum {sm, md, lg} -> px 24/32/40, and a separate `sizePx` double? override; `ring` is an AvatarRing record (color, width) as a single outset shadow layer applied by the caller; `badge` takes an AvatarBadge value object (fill, child?).
api.web: Avatar size prop: "default"|"sm"|"lg" via data-size attribute, resolving through data-[size=lg]:size-10 / data-[size=sm]:size-6 classes; AvatarBadge is a plain span the caller positions with className (no dedicated API for ring or fill beyond raw Tailwind classes); AvatarBadge also carries an unported `bg-blend-color` class and a `group-data-[size=sm]:[&>svg]:hidden` rule for a child glyph.

ORIGINAL: Flutter's own doc comment records two explicit 'Not ported' items on AvatarBadge: `bg-blend-color` (needs a second background layer to blend with, and the Flutter fill is flat) and `group-data-[size=sm]:[&>svg]:hidden` (needs a glyph child, and no corpus badge has one). Both are real API-surface gaps -- a caller who puts a glyph in a `sm` AvatarBadge on web gets it auto-hidden; on Flutter it always renders, since AvatarBadge.child is unconditional. states.flutter: Image?.errorBuilder falls back to SizedBox.shrink() on decode failure, letting the fallback content already painted underneath show through -- same behaviour as 'missing or still loading'.
states.web: Radix AvatarPrimitive shows AvatarFallback whenever the image is missing, still loading, or fails to decode, and swaps to AvatarImage once it resolves successfully.

disabled.flutter: Avatar is a StatelessWidget with no enabled/disabled concept -- it is a display-only identity mark.
disabled.web: Avatar/AvatarImage/AvatarFallback declare no disabled prop or data-disabled hook.
disabled.note: A passive identity mark has no disabled state to compare on either platform.

interaction.flutter: No pointer, keyboard, or focus handling anywhere in Avatar, AvatarBadge, AvatarGroup, or AvatarGroupCount -- pure paint.
interaction.web: None of the six exported pieces attach event handlers or tabIndex; any interactivity is the caller's responsibility (e.g. wrapping the avatar in a button).
interaction.note: Avatar is non-interactive on both platforms by design.

semantics.flutter: Initials render through StyledText inside a Center with no explicit Semantics wrapper, so a screen reader reads the fallback text or, once an image loads, nothing distinguishing -- same as the web's untagged /fallback span; a caller supplying an alt-equivalent must do so via its own context.
semantics.web: AvatarPrimitive.Image forwards whatever alt/aria props the caller passes (none supplied by the base component itself); AvatarFallback is a plain span with no implicit role.
